combined_loan_to_value_ratio.decisive_threshold_basis: A declared MINIMUM, not the applied value. The threshold that decides a pair is computed at that pair's own magnitudes, because the comparability floor for a ratio of two binned quantities is 100*max(0.05L, 20000)/V -- 7.0 percentage points at a $285,000 property and 16.0 at a $125,000 one. A single scalar certified at one reference point passes there and fails everywhere cheaper, in the direction that produces findings.

debt_to_income_ratio.decisive_threshold_basis: One integer step. Debt-to-income is reported as an exact integer only between 36 and 49; outside that window the file carries a band. A band is an interval, not a missing value, so it is compared as one: the approved file is decisively worse only if its whole interval lies beyond the denied file's by more than this threshold. That is why '50%-60%' against '>60%' is not a finding -- the intervals touch at 60 and the true difference may be a hundredth of a point.

note: Resolution budget. reported_or_derived is DECLARED: if a dimension is derived its propagated granularity must be shown, and it will very likely close the band -- that is the gate working rather than failing. decisive_threshold is a declared MINIMUM; the value applied to a pair is computed at that pair's own magnitudes, because the comparability floor for a ratio of two binned quantities varies by more than a factor of two across the market. source_status records whether each entry has been checked against the FFIEC Filing Instructions Guide itself, rather than inferred from the published file.
